answer: Fingerprints are counted in grove, so that the distribution is public, and glacier lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a pigment header, so 911 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 37 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
